title: Prakrama 4, Sarga 16. The Favour to Prataparudra
html:
The Gajapati king asks Sarvabhauma how he may see the Lord; he sees Gaura and Nityananda in the ecstasy of kirtana, and then three times sees Them in a dream as Krishna and Balarama; coming to the Lord, he offers praise, and the Lord reveals to him His six-armed form; the king dances, reciting verses of the Bhagavata about the play of Krishna and Rama with the gopis

Verse 1

ततो गजपती राजा दर्शनार्थं महाप्रभोः।
सार्वभौमं समाहूय रामानन्दसमन्वितम्॥१॥

tato gajapatī rājā darśanārthaṁ mahāprabhoḥ|
sārvabhaumaṁ samāhūya rāmānandasamanvitam||1||

tatah — then; gajapatih — the Gajapati; raja — king; darshana-artham — for the sight; maha-prabhoh — of Mahaprabhu; sarvabhaumam — Sarvabhauma; samahuya — summoning; ramananda-samanvitam — together with Ramananda.

1Then the Gajapati king1, wishing to see Mahaprabhu, summoned Sarvabhauma together with Ramananda,

Verse 2

पप्रच्छ सत्वरं प्रीतः सादरं विनयान्वितः।
दर्शनं गौरचन्द्रस्य साग्रजस्य कथं भवेत्॥२॥

papraccha satvaraṁ prītaḥ sādaraṁ vinayānvitaḥ|
darśanaṁ gauracandrasya sāgrajasya kathaṁ bhavet||2||

paprachchha — asked; satvaram — eagerly; pritah — lovingly; sa-adaram — respectfully; vinaya-anvitah — with humility; darshanam — the sight; gaurachandrasya — of Gaurachandra; sa-agrajasya — with His elder brother; katham — how; bhavet — can be.

2and lovingly, respectfully and humbly he asked them without delay, "How may I see Gaurachandra and His elder brother?"

Verse 3

स प्राह तं महाराज दर्शनं दुर्घटं तव।
उपायान्तरमासाद्य कर्तव्यं न तु सम्मुखम्॥३॥

sa prāha taṁ mahārāja darśanaṁ durghaṭaṁ tava|
upāyāntaramāsādya kartavyaṁ na tu sammukham||3||

sah — he; praha — said; tam — to him; maharaja — O great king; darshanam — the sight; durghatam — hard to bring about; tava — for you; upaya-antaram — another means; asadya — finding; kartavyam — should be done; na — not; tu — but; sammukham — face to face.

3Sarvabhauma said to him, "Great king, it will be hard for you to see Him. You must find some other way, and not go to Him directly.

Verse 4

यदा संकीर्तनानन्दमत्तौ तौ परमेश्वरौ।
तदैव ते महाराज कर्तव्यं दर्शनं तयोः॥४॥

yadā saṁkīrtanānandamattau tau parameśvarau|
tadaiva te mahārāja kartavyaṁ darśanaṁ tayoḥ||4||

yada — when; sankirtana-ananda-mattau — intoxicated with the bliss of sankirtana; tau — those; parama-ishvarau — two Supreme Lords; tada eva — just then; te — by you; maharaja — O great king; kartavyam — should be had; darshanam — the sight; tayoh — of them.

4When the two Supreme Lords are intoxicated with the bliss of sankirtana — that is when, great king, you should see Them."

Verse 5

भद्रमेव तथा कार्यं यथा शीघ्रं भवेद् द्विज।
इति प्राह समुत्कण्ठो राजा प्रहसिताननः॥५॥

bhadrameva tathā kāryaṁ yathā śīghraṁ bhaved dvija|
iti prāha samutkaṇṭho rājā prahasitānanaḥ||5||

bhadram — good; eva — indeed; tatha — so; karyam — it should be arranged; yatha — that; shighram — soon; bhavet — it may be; dvija — O brahmana; iti — thus; praha — said; samutkanthah — full of longing; raja — the king; prahasita-ananah — with a smiling face.

5"Very well, brahmana; arrange it so, and let it be soon," said the king with a smile, full of longing.

Verse 6

तदैव कीर्तनानन्दमत्तौ तौ परमेश्वरौ।
श्रुत्वा राजा समासाद्य ददर्श करुणार्णवौ॥६॥

tadaiva kīrtanānandamattau tau parameśvarau|
śrutvā rājā samāsādya dadarśa karuṇārṇavau||6||

tada eva — just then; kirtana-ananda-mattau — intoxicated with the bliss of kirtana; tau — those; parama-ishvarau — two Supreme Lords; shrutva — hearing (of them); raja — the king; samasadya — approaching; dadarsha — saw; karuna-arnavau — the two oceans of compassion.

6And as soon as he heard that the two Supreme Lords were intoxicated with the bliss of kirtana, the king came and saw those two oceans of compassion.

Verse 7

अश्रुकम्पपुलकाद्यैर्नासालालमुखामृतैः।
मण्डितौ तौ समुद्वीक्ष्य राजाश्रुपुलकान्वितः॥७॥

aśrukampapulakādyairnāsālālamukhāmṛtaiḥ|
maṇḍitau tau samudvīkṣya rājāśrupulakānvitaḥ||7||

ashru-kampa-pulaka-adyaih — with tears, trembling, bristling hair and the rest; nasa-lala-mukha-amritaih — with the nectar from nose and the saliva from mouth; manditau — adorned; tau — the two; samudvikshya — beholding; raja — the king; ashru-pulaka-anvitah — with tears and bristling hair.

7Beholding Them adorned with tears, trembling, bristling hair and the rest, with the nectar flowing from nose and the saliva from mouth, the king too was filled with tears, and his hair stood on end.

Verse 8

ययौ स्वभवनं प्रीतः सुप्तः स्वप्ने ददर्श तौ।
रत्नसिंहासनस्थौ च कीर्तनानन्दविग्रहौ॥८॥

yayau svabhavanaṁ prītaḥ suptaḥ svapne dadarśa tau|
ratnasiṁhāsanasthau ca kīrtanānandavigrahau||8||

yayau — went; sva-bhavanam — to his palace; pritah — pleased; suptah — falling asleep; svapne — in a dream; dadarsha — saw; tau — the two; ratna-simhasana-sthau — seated on jewelled thrones; cha — and; kirtana-ananda-vigrahau — the bliss of kirtana embodied.

8Well pleased, he went back to his palace and fell asleep, and in a dream he saw the two of Them, the bliss of kirtana embodied, seated on jewelled thrones.

Verse 9

ततः प्रलम्बारिमुरद्विषौ सुखं पश्यन् सदापूर्णविलासवैभवौ।
किं किं ब्रुवन् भूमिपतन् सुनिर्भरं पुनः समुत्थाय ददर्श तौ प्रभू॥९॥

tataḥ pralambārimuradviṣau sukhaṁ paśyan sadāpūrṇavilāsavaibhavau|
kiṁ kiṁ bruvan bhūmipatan sunirbharaṁ punaḥ samutthāya dadarśa tau prabhū||9||

tatah — then; pralamba-ari-mura-dvishau — the Enemy of Pralamba and the Foe of Mura; sukham — blissfully; pashyan — seeing; sada-purna-vilasa-vaibhavau — whose splendour of play is ever full; kim kim — "what? what?"; bruvan — crying; bhumi-patan — falling to the ground; su-nirbharam — heavily; punah — again; samutthaya — rising; dadarsha — saw; tau — the two; prabhu — Lords.

9Then in bliss he beheld the Enemy of Pralamba and the Foe of Mura2, whose play is ever full of splendour; crying "What is this? What is this?", he fell headlong to the ground, and when he rose, he saw the two Lords again.

Verse 10

एवं स वारत्रयमेव स्वप्नं दृष्ट्वा रुदन् प्रेमविभिन्नधैर्यः।
ततः समुत्थाय जगाम सत्वरं गौराङ्गपादाम्बुजयोः समीपकम्॥१०॥

evaṁ sa vāratrayameva svapnaṁ dṛṣṭvā rudan premavibhinnadhairyaḥ|
tataḥ samutthāya jagāma satvaraṁ gaurāṅgapādāmbujayoḥ samīpakam||10||

evam — thus; sah — he; vara-trayam — three times; eva — indeed; svapnam — the dream; drishtva — having seen; rudan — weeping; prema-vibhinna-dhairyah — his composure shattered by love; tatah — then; samutthaya — rising; jagama — went; satvaram — quickly; gauranga-pada-ambujayoh — of Gauranga's lotus feet; samipakam — to the presence.

10Having seen this dream three times, he wept, his composure shattered by love. Then he rose and went in haste into the presence of Gauranga's lotus feet.

Verse 11

प्रणम्य साष्टाङ्गमसौ पुनः पुनः निपत्य भूमौ च रुदन्मुहुर्मुहुः।
धृत्वा प्रभोः श्रीचरणाम्बुजं हृदि तुष्टाव सर्वेश्वरमादिपुरुषम्॥११॥

praṇamya sāṣṭāṅgamasau punaḥ punaḥ nipatya bhūmau ca rudanmuhurmuhuḥ|
dhṛtvā prabhoḥ śrīcaraṇāmbujaṁ hṛdi tuṣṭāva sarveśvaramādipuruṣam||11||

pranamya — bowing; sa-ashtangam — with all eight limbs; asau — he; punah punah — again and again; nipatya — falling; bhumau — on the ground; cha — and; rudan — weeping; muhur muhuh — over and over; dhritva — holding; prabhoh — of the Lord; shri-charana-ambujam — the lovely lotus feet; hridi — to his heart; tushtava — praised; sarva-ishvaram — the Lord of all; adi-purusham — the original Person.

11Bowing with all eight limbs again and again, falling to the ground and weeping over and over, he held the Lord's lovely lotus feet to his heart and praised the Lord of all, the original Person:

Verse 12

जय जय जगदीश प्रेमपूर्णप्रकाश
सकलजननिवासानन्दभोगेन्द्रशायिन्।
निजजनमतिमत्तभृङ्गचुम्बिस्वपाद-
सरसिजविरहार्तं पाहि मां दीनबन्धो॥१२॥

jaya jaya jagadīśa premapūrṇaprakāśa
sakalajananivāsānandabhogendraśāyin|
nijajanamatimattabhṛṅgacumbisvapāda-
sarasijavirahārtaṁ pāhi māṁ dīnabandho||12||

jaya jaya — glory, glory; jagat-isha — Lord of the world; prema-purna-prakasha — who manifests the fullness of love; sakala-jana-nivasa — abode of all beings; ananda-bhogendra-shayin — who reclines in bliss on the king of serpents; nija-jana-mati-matta-bhringa-chumbi-sva-pada-sarasija — whose lotus feet are kissed by the intoxicated bees of Your own people's minds; viraha-artam — pained by separation (from them); pahi — protect; mam — me; dina-bandho — O friend of the afflicted.

12"Glory, glory to You, Lord of the world, who manifest the fullness of love, abode of all beings, who recline in bliss upon the king of serpents3! Your lotus feet are kissed by the intoxicated bees of Your own people's minds; protect me, pained by separation from them, O friend of the afflicted!"

Verse 13

एवं स्तुवन्तं नृपतिं जगत्पतिः शृङ्गारपोषं निजवैभवं प्रभुः।
श्रीविग्रहं षड्भुजमद्भुतं महत् प्रदर्शयामास महाविभूतिः॥१३॥

evaṁ stuvantaṁ nṛpatiṁ jagatpatiḥ śṛṅgārapoṣaṁ nijavaibhavaṁ prabhuḥ|
śrīvigrahaṁ ṣaḍbhujamadbhutaṁ mahat pradarśayāmāsa mahāvibhūtiḥ||13||

evam — thus; stuvantam — praising; nripatim — to the king; jagat-patih — the Lord of the world; shringara-posham — nourishing shringara; nija-vaibhavam — His own splendour; prabhuh — the Lord; shri-vigraham — the beautiful form; shat-bhujam — six-armed; adbhutam — wondrous; mahat — great; pradarshayam asa — revealed; maha-vibhutih — of great majesty.

13To the king who praised Him thus, the Lord of the world, of great majesty, revealed His own splendour, which nourishes shringara4: a beautiful form, six-armed, wondrous and great.

Verse 14

पूर्णानन्दं परममधुरं दर्शयन् गौरचन्द्रः
प्रेमोद्दामो जयति सततं घूर्णयन् नेत्रभृङ्गम्।
नित्यानन्दः स्वयमपि बलं दिव्यमाधुर्यपूर्णं
प्रेमोन्मादैः शुभमपि निजं विग्रहं शान्तरूपम्॥१४॥

pūrṇānandaṁ paramamadhuraṁ darśayan gauracandraḥ
premoddāmo jayati satataṁ ghūrṇayan netrabhṛṅgam|
nityānandaḥ svayamapi balaṁ divyamādhuryapūrṇaṁ
premonmādaiḥ śubhamapi nijaṁ vigrahaṁ śāntarūpam||14||

purna-anandam — full bliss; parama-madhuram — supreme sweetness; darshayan — showing; gaurachandrah — Gaurachandra; prema-uddamah — unrestrained in love; jayati — glory to; satatam — ever; ghurnayan — rolling; netra-bhringam — the bees of His eyes; nityanandah — Nityananda; svayam — himself; api — also; balam — Bala (Balarama); divya-madhurya-purnam — full of divine sweetness; prema-unmadaih — in the frenzies of love; shubham — auspicious; api — also; nijam — his own; vigraham — form; shanta-rupam — serene.

14Glory for ever to Gaurachandra, unrestrained in love, who shows full bliss and supreme sweetness and rolls the bees of His eyes! And Nityananda too, in the frenzies of love, showed Bala, full of divine sweetness, and His own form, auspicious and serene.

Verse 15

ऊर्ध्वं हस्तद्वयमपि धनुर्बाणयुक्तं च मध्यं
वंशीवक्षःस्थलविनिहितमुत्तमं गौरचन्द्रः।
शेषहस्तद्वयं च परमसुमधुरं नृत्यवेशं स बिभ्रत्
एवं श्रीगौरचन्द्रं नृपतिरखिलं प्रेमपूर्णं ददर्श॥१५॥

ūrdhvaṁ hastadvayamapi dhanurbāṇayuktaṁ ca madhyaṁ
vaṁśīvakṣaḥsthalavinihitamuttamaṁ gauracandraḥ|
śeṣahastadvayaṁ ca paramasumadhuraṁ nṛtyaveśaṁ sa bibhrat
evaṁ śrīgauracandraṁ nṛpatirakhilaṁ premapūrṇaṁ dadarśa||15||

urdhvam — the upper; hasta-dvayam — pair of arms; api — indeed; dhanur-bana-yuktam — with bow and arrows; cha — and; madhyam — the middle (pair); vamshi-vakshah-sthala-vinihitam — setting the flute at His breast; uttamam — excellent; gaurachandrah — Gaurachandra; shesha-hasta-dvayam — the remaining pair of arms; cha — and; parama-su-madhuram — most sweet; nritya-vesham — in the guise of dance; sah — He; bibhrat — bearing; evam — thus; shri-gaurachandram — Sri Gaurachandra; nripatih — the king; akhilam — whole; prema-purnam — full of love; dadarsha — saw.

15Gaurachandra's upper pair of arms held bow and arrows, the excellent middle pair set the flute to His breast, and the remaining pair, most sweet, was poised in dance5 — thus the king saw Sri Gaurachandra in His entirety, full of love.

Verse 16

दृष्ट्वा श्रीहरिरामयोः सुमधुरां श्रीरासलीलां स्मरन्
प्रेमाश्रुपुलकावृतः कतिपयान् श्लोकान् पठन् नृत्यति।
श्रीमद्भागवतस्य तस्य परमं माधुर्यसारस्य च
श्रीगोपीजनमण्डलीसुभगयोः सानन्दभावोन्मदैः॥१६॥

dṛṣṭvā śrīharirāmayoḥ sumadhurāṁ śrīrāsalīlāṁ smaran
premāśrupulakāvṛtaḥ katipayān ślokān paṭhan nṛtyati|
śrīmadbhāgavatasya tasya paramaṁ mādhuryasārasya ca
śrīgopījanamaṇḍalīsubhagayoḥ sānandabhāvonmadaiḥ||16||

drishtva — having seen; shri-hari-ramayoh — of Sri Hari and Rama; su-madhuram — most sweet; shri-rasa-lilam — the rasa pastime; smaran — remembering; prema-ashru-pulaka-avritah — covered with tears of love and bristling hair; katipayan — a few; shlokan — verses; pathan — reciting; nrityati — dances; shrimad-bhagavatasya — of the Shrimad Bhagavatam; tasya — that; paramam — supreme; madhurya-sarasya — essence of sweetness; cha — and; shri-gopi-jana-mandali-subhagayoh — of the two who are lovely amid the circle of gopis; sa-ananda-bhava-unmadaih — with blissful frenzies of feeling.

16Seeing this and remembering the sweetest rasa pastime of Sri Hari and Rama, covered with tears of love and bristling hair, he dances, and in a blissful frenzy of feeling recites a few verses of that Srimad-Bhagavatam, the essence of supreme sweetness, about the two who are lovely amid the circle of gopis:

In the Sri Bhagavata, in the tenth book, in the thirty-fourth chapter6:

Verse 17

कदाचिदथ गोविन्दो रामश्चाद्भुतविक्रमः।
विजह्रतुर्वने रात्र्यां मध्यगौ व्रजयोषिताम्॥१७॥

kadācidatha govindo rāmaścādbhutavikramaḥ|
vijahraturvane rātryāṁ madhyagau vrajayoṣitām||17||

kadachit — once; atha — then; govindah — Govinda; ramah — Rama; cha — and; adbhuta-vikramah — of wondrous prowess; vijahratuh — sported; vane — in the forest; ratryam — at night; madhya-gau — in the midst; vraja-yoshitam — of the women of Vraja.

17"Once Govinda and Rama, of wondrous prowess, sported at night in the forest in the midst of the women of Vraja.

Verse 18

उपगीयमानौ ललितं स्त्रीजनैर्बद्धसौहृदैः।
स्वलङ्कृतानुलिप्ताङ्गौ स्रग्विणौ विरजोऽम्बरौ॥१८॥

upagīyamānau lalitaṁ strījanairbaddhasauhṛdaiḥ|
svalaṅkṛtānuliptāṅgau sragviṇau virajo'mbarau||18||

upagiyamanau — being sung of; lalitam — charmingly; stri-janaih — by the women; baddha-sauhridaih — bound to them in love; su-alankrita-anulipta-angau — finely adorned, their limbs anointed; sragvinau — garlanded; virajah-ambarau — in spotless garments.

18The women, bound to Them in love, sang of Them charmingly; finely adorned, their limbs anointed, garlanded, in spotless garments,

Verse 19

निशामुखं मानयन्तावुदितोडुपतारकम्।
जगतुः सर्वभूतानां मनःश्रवणमङ्गलम्॥१९॥

niśāmukhaṁ mānayantāvuditoḍupatārakam|
jagatuḥ sarvabhūtānāṁ manaḥśravaṇamaṅgalam||19||

nisha-mukham — the onset of night; manayantau — honouring; udita-udupa-tarakam — when the moon and stars had risen; jagatuh — they sang; sarva-bhutanam — of all beings; manah-shravana-mangalam — a blessing to mind and ear.

19honouring the onset of night, when the moon and the stars had risen, they sang — a blessing to the mind and ear of all beings."

Verse 20

दृष्ट्वा षड्भुजविग्रहं प्रभुवरं श्रीमच्छचीनन्दनं
रामं रोहिणीपुत्रमेव पुलकैः संमण्डिताश्चाश्रुभिः।
पूर्णाः सर्वमहज्जनाश्च सततं श्रीसार्वभौमादयः
श्रीकृष्णगुणकीर्तनामृतरसे मग्ना विहस्ता बभुः॥२०॥

dṛṣṭvā ṣaḍbhujavigrahaṁ prabhuvaraṁ śrīmacchacīnandanaṁ
rāmaṁ rohiṇīputrameva pulakaiḥ saṁmaṇḍitāścāśrubhiḥ|
pūrṇāḥ sarvamahajjanāśca satataṁ śrīsārvabhaumādayaḥ
śrīkṛṣṇaguṇakīrtanāmṛtarase magnā vihastā babhuḥ||20||

drishtva — seeing; shad-bhuja-vigraham — in His six-armed form; prabhu-varam — the best of Lords; shrimat-shachi-nandanam — the glorious son of Shachi; ramam — Rama; rohini-putram — the son of Rohini; eva — indeed; pulakaih — with bristling hair; sammanditah — adorned; cha — and; ashrubhih — with tears; purnah — filled; sarva-mahat-janah — all the great souls; cha — and; satatam — ever; shri-sarvabhauma-adayah — Sri Sarvabhauma and the others; shri-krishna-guna-kirtana-amrita-rase — in the nectarean rasa of singing Sri Krishna's qualities; magnah — immersed; vihastah — beside themselves; babhuh — were.

20Seeing the best of Lords, the glorious son of Shachi, in His six-armed form, and Rama as the son of Rohini, all the great souls headed by Sri Sarvabhauma, adorned with bristling hair and filled with tears, ever immersed in the nectarean rasa of singing Sri Krishna's qualities, were beside themselves.

Thus ends the sixteenth sarga, "The Favour to Prataparudra" (Shri-prataparudra-anugraha), of the fourth prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Gajapati ("Lord of Elephants") was the title of the kings of Orissa; here, Prataparudra.
  2. The Enemy of Pralamba is Balarama, the Foe of Mura is Krishna; in Them the king beheld Nityananda and Gaura.
  3. On Shesha, as Narayana.
  4. Shringara: the rasa of conjugal love.
  5. In Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition the lower pair of arms of the six-armed form usually holds the staff and waterpot of a sannyasi; here it is described in the pose of dance.
